concept_definition: in physics, the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred, measured in watts.
the indefinite continued progress of existence; a measurable period during which an action or condition exists or continues
one of two equal parts of something
a piece or segment of something
a particular spot, moment, or detail
a mathematical value or quantity
physical power or mental resilience
power or energy as an attribute of action; in physics, an influence that causes an object to undergo a change in speed, direction, or shape
the amount of space between two points
a number or numerical symbol
the rate at which something moves
a position on a scale of quantity or quality
a number of people or things gathered together
the measurement of something from end to end
the relative extent of something
a portion of something
the measure of how heavy something is
the quality of being hot; thermal energy transferred from a hotter to a cooler body
continuous force exerted on or against something
two individuals together; a small number of
a group of twelve
a large number or multitude of something
a measure or frequency of something per unit of time or other quantity
a large body of matter; in physics, the quantity of matter in a body
a large number or amount of something
a small piece or amount of something
the act of determining the total number of something; the resulting total
Each of four equal parts into which something can be divided.
A group of related things that belong together or are used together.
the mathematical process of combining two or more numbers to find their total.
a quantity of something.
the amount remaining after a deduction or payment.
the act of evaluating two or more things to note similarities and differences.
the mathematical process of splitting a number into equal parts.
the extent or scope between upper and lower limits.
a graduated system of measurement or classification.
a single quantity regarded as a standard for measurement.
A covering or layer of a substance spread over a surface.
The amount of space that a substance or object occupies.
The best performance or most remarkable event of its kind.
The remaining part of something.
the maximum legal speed on a road
the average level of the ocean surface
the average number of years a person is expected to live
the general level of prices for daily necessities
the percentage charged or paid on money
the value of one currency against another
the lowest wage an employer may legally pay
The mathematical operation of combining equal groups to find a total, represented by multiplying numbers or quantities.
A number or system based on ten, especially one using digits 0–9 and place values that are powers of ten.
The trigonometric function equal to the sine of an angle divided by its cosine.
The number obtained by dividing one number by another.
An unlimited extent, amount, or number; something without an end or limit.
An unbounded mathematical quantity or concept, represented by the symbol ∞, that is greater than every finite quantity in a relevant context.
The exponent to which a specified base must be raised to produce a given number.
The mathematical operation of taking one number or quantity away from another.
A number or symbol written above and to the right of another number or symbol to indicate the power to which it is raised.
The product of all positive integers from 1 up to a given positive integer; written as n!.
A rearrangement of the elements of a set or sequence into a particular order.
The mathematical operation of raising a number or quantity to a power.
A number by which another number is divided; a factor of the dividend in a division operation.
An extremely small quantity or amount; especially a quantity approaching zero in mathematics.
The number of elements in a set, whether finite or infinite.
A scalar associated with a linear transformation or square matrix such that there is a nonzero vector that the transformation maps to the scalar multiple of itself.

A measure of how two variables change together: a positive value indicates that they tend to increase or decrease together, while a negative value indicates that one tends to increase as the other decreases.
A function whose derivative is equal to a given function; an indefinite integral.
In mathematics, the set of values that a function is declared to map into; the function’s target set, which may contain values that the function does not actually attain.
A discrete, indivisible amount of a physical quantity, especially energy, as described by quantum theory.
A numerical measure of the size or strength of a quantity, especially in mathematics or physics.
The speed of an object in a specified direction.
A value obtained by measuring something, usually expressed with a number and a unit.
The rate at which a particular word, sound, letter, or other item occurs in a body of text or data.
The number of times a particular value or range of values occurs in a statistical dataset.
The ratio of useful output to total input in a process, machine, or system, often expressed as a percentage.
The proportion of a population that has a particular disease, condition, or characteristic at a given time or during a specified period.
An interval between two musical notes in which the higher note has twice the frequency of the lower note; specifically, a span of eight diatonic notes.
The proportion of light or other radiation reflected by a surface, especially a planet, moon, or other astronomical body, expressed as a value from zero to one or as a percentage.
A number or amount greater than that of any other option, but not necessarily more than half of the total; the largest share.
The amount of money repaid for an expense or payment.
The amount by which one quantity is greater or less than another; the result of subtracting one number from another.
The complete amount or number resulting from adding or combining parts.
A number calculated by adding a set of numbers and dividing the total by how many numbers there are; the arithmetic mean.
A typical amount, level, standard, or value calculated from or representing a group.
The result obtained by multiplying two or more numbers or quantities.
More than half of a total number or amount; the greater part.
The number of votes or members by which one side exceeds the other in a decision or election.
The amount of money required to buy, make, or do something.
The amount of a specified substance contained in something.
The measurement of how tall someone or something is, especially from bottom to top.
The size, area, length, or range of something.
The amount of a substance that fills a cup.
A number or set of numbers representing points gained in a game, test, or competition.
The desire or need for a product or service among consumers, often considered in relation to its availability or price.
In chess, a tempo is the time or move advantage a player gains or loses, often by making a move that forces the opponent to respond.
In chess, the time control is the amount of time each player is allowed for a game or for a specified number of moves.
In tennis, love is a score of zero points in a game.
In baseball, the count is the number of balls and strikes recorded against a batter during an at-bat.
A statistic in baseball that measures how often a batter gets a hit, calculated by dividing hits by official at-bats.
In cricket, a run is one point scored when the batters complete a run between the wickets or score in another permitted way.
In golf, the standard number of strokes an expert golfer is expected to take to complete a hole or course.
In golf, a numerical measure of a player's ability used to adjust scores so players of different skill levels can compete fairly.
In go, a number of points added to White’s score to compensate for Black’s first-move advantage.
In boxing, the weight class for fighters above the sport’s heavyweight limit in lower divisions; its minimum weight limit is 200 pounds in professional boxing.
A boxing weight class for fighters whose weight falls within the division’s prescribed limits.
A boxing weight class for fighters whose weight is above the lightweight limit and no more than 147 pounds (66.7 kilograms) in professional boxing.
A boxing weight class for fighters who weigh no more than the featherweight limit, below the lightweight class.
A boxing weight class for fighters weighing up to 118 pounds (53.5 kilograms) in professional boxing.
A boxing weight division for fighters weighing no more than 112 pounds (about 50.8 kilograms).
A boxing weight division for fighters who weigh no more than 135 pounds (61.2 kilograms) in professional boxing.
The rate at which a cyclist turns the pedals, usually measured in revolutions per minute.
A rank or grade above the beginner levels in martial arts or go, typically awarded to advanced practitioners.
In backgammon, a pip is one point of distance that a checker moves when traveling between board points.
A student rank below dan in a martial art or wrestling ranking system.
